question: At each saved support witness (placement, posture search, directed shift, and iterated shift poses), with every equality row strict and friction unchanged, what uniform scale s on the declared tendon tension limits admits static support? The iterative run floored the full-support residual near 0.2 with tensions saturated at fmax; this measures the deficit directly.
hypothesis: If some witness yields s <= 1, declared tension authority suffices at that fixed geometry; a finite s > 1 quantifies the force deficit of the transferred tension limits; 'unreachable at any scale' means contact geometry alone cannot cover the root+passive rows regardless of muscle force.
units: Native MuJoCo model units; the margin s is dimensionless (multiple of the declared tension limits)
controls: no physics is re-derived: only saved support witnesses from the four declared evidence sets are replayed
the friction diamond, equality rows, scaling and solver are byte-identical to the support LP; only the tension bound becomes s*fmax
a witness whose margin LP is undecided is recorded as unresolved, never as physical infeasibility
success_criterion: Every saved witness replays a decided margin LP; per-witness s and tension vectors reproduce under re-solve; witness sets cover every saved support array and carry evidence_saved linkage; the aggregate outcome follows the declared rules.
falsification: s <= 1 on any witness rejects 'declared tension authority is insufficient at this geometry'. A finite s > 1 is a local statement about saved geometries; s = infinity identifies structural contact/rank limits independent of muscle force.

parameters.question: With all equality rows strict and friction unchanged, what uniform scale s on declared tension limits admits static support at each saved witness?
parameters.variables: tensions f, contact forces r, scalar tension-authority scale s; constraints f_j <= s*fmax_j, f >= 0, friction diamond, T f + C r = b on every row
parameters.scope: Fixed-geometry algebraic screen on saved witnesses; a finite s* measures the force deficit of the transferred tension limits, not a physical posture or a biological claim
